subject: Electromotive force
hook: ELECTROMOTIVE FORCE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Despite its name, electromotive force is not a physical force at all, and the term has been formally deprecated by international standards in favor of source voltage.
angle_support: However, electromotive force itself is not a physical force, and ISO/IEC standards have deprecated the term in favor of source voltage or source tension instead
title: Why Electromotive Force is a Lie
description: Despite its common name, electromotive force has nothing to do with physical forces. It is simply an energy transfer per unit of charge, leading international standards to officially move away from the term.
narration: ELECTROMOTIVE FORCE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a physical force pushing electrons through a wire. It was closer to energy transfer. It is not a force at all; it is actually energy. International standards have formally deprecated the term entirely. Scientists now prefer the label source voltage. It describes work done per charge, measured in volts, rather than a literal mechanical push exerted by a physical, classical force. Names can be misleading, especially when they imply hidden physical pushing.
